text:
The day before Jiri Kulich scored at Philadelphia, The Hockey News ran the headline "Sabres Potentially Open To Sending Kulich To The AHL To Find His Game." Bleacher Report's Joe Yerdon put the goal plainly: "Kulich really needed a lift and that'll do it."

It's been that kind of start. Kulich has 2 goals and 4 points in 14 games, his ice time is down to about 14 minutes over his last ten, and he has no power-play points. The underlying play is better than the line. Buffalo takes 52.4% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, about 4 points better than without him, and his teammates have scored 3.5 fewer goals than expected while he's out there.

The 28th pick of 2022 scored 24 goals in 62 AHL games at Rochester before reaching the NHL, and NHL EDGE puts his top shot in the 80th percentile of forwards. Our talent range is wide for a player with this little NHL track record. Watch the minutes: they'll say more about his place than any single game.
